newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand to unveil terms for BBC sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Thailand to unveil terms for BBC sell-off.

text.p: Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan was expected on Tuesday to announce revised terms for a new round of bidding for troubled Bangkok Bank of Commerce, a member of a panel controlling the bank said.

"The minister is going to announce his plans for the Finance Ministry tomorrow, and that will include what is going to happen with BBC," an executive working with state-contolled committee looking after the bank's affairs told Reuters on Monday.
"Officials from the Bank of Thailand have submitted to the minister asking for a new bidding process and a new bidding framework," he said.
The announcement follows the breakdown of talks between the BBC committee and prospective buyer Sitca Investment and Securities.

The central bank used its Financial Institutions Rehabilitation Fund, to which Thai financiers make annual contributions, to take a controlling stake in BBC in May when it was found to be carrying 85 billion baht (US$3.25 billion) in non-performing loans.

The revised bidding terms are said to include a waiver of crossholding rules between financial institutions and a commitment from the authorities to assist with handling of an as yet undeclared portion of the bank's bad debt burden.
Thai firms must be lead bidders in the new round although foreign backers of bids headed by local firms will likely be permitted.
"It will be limited to Thai financial institutions only since the fund took money from financial instuitutions, then they have to give them the chance to rescue it," he said.

Other terms being considered by the minister are said to include specific prices linked to the size of stake the rescuer is prepared to take shares and a revised time frame for the full rehabilitation of the bank, previously set at seven years.
The new bidding framework is will not prevent failed bidders which include Nithipat Capital Plc NPAT. BK and Sitca from resubmitting bids, the executive said.
